q: What is the maximum number of years an audit partner can serve on a non-PIE audit before familiarity threat assessment is required under standard guidelines?
When is an indirect financial interest in an audit client prohibited for an audit team member?
o: When the indirect financial interest is material to either the individual or the client entity
Only when the interest exceeds fifty percent of the total assets of the audit firm
Under no circumstances, as all indirect interests are automatically permitted
Only when the audit client specifically requests that the holding be sold off
e: An indirect financial interest in an audit client is prohibited if it is material to either the investor or the client entity.

q: Under the principle of professional behavior, what specific duty is placed on a professional accountant?
o: Comply with relevant laws and regulations and avoid any conduct that might discredit the profession
Accept every commercial client regardless of reputational risk or lack of technical capability
Ensure the accounting firm reports a growing profit margin across every operational quarter
Refrain from competing against other professional firms in open public sector tenders
e: Professional behavior requires compliance with relevant laws and regulations and avoiding any conduct that the accountant knows or should know might discredit the profession.

q: How should an audit firm handle overdue audit fees from a prior year before issuing the current year audit report?
o: Evaluate whether the overdue fees resemble a loan to the client, creating a self-interest threat
Forgive the overdue debt entirely in exchange for an equity interest in the client business
Ignore the overdue fees, as historical debts have no bearing on current year objectivity
Charge exorbitant interest rates on the unpaid balance to punish the client management
e: Overdue fees can create a self-interest threat if they are significant, as they may be perceived as a loan to the client, threatening independence if unpaid before the next report is issued.

q: Memorize the pairings between each whistleblowing term and its definition:

pairs.Protected Disclosure: Report of wrongdoing shielded by statutory legal immunity
pairs.Escalation Path: Step-by-step reporting route through internal governance
pairs.External Reporting: Disclosing non-compliance to regulatory or enforcement agencies

q: Which of the following is NOT an element of the reasonable and informed third party test?
options: Weighing all specific facts and circumstances
Considering the perspective of an objective external observer
Assuming the auditor has perfect omniscient knowledge
Evaluating the significance of threats and safeguards
correct: Assuming the auditor has perfect omniscient knowledge

q: Under the IESBA Code, what safeguard might mitigate a familiarity threat arising from long association on a non-PIE audit?
o: Rotating the engagement partner or key audit personnel off the engagement team
Increasing the engagement partner billable hourly rate by twenty-five percent
Eliminating the requirement to prepare audit working paper documentation
Allowing the client finance director to review and sign off on audit testing procedures
e: Safeguards to address familiarity threats include rotating personnel off the audit team, bringing in an independent reviewing partner, or performing regular external quality reviews.

What is the ethical implication when an audit firm partner joins an audit client as Chief Executive Officer shortly after leaving the firm?
o: Significant familiarity, intimidation, and self-review threats arise regarding the audit firm
The firm is legally obliged to transfer all its equity to the former partner company
No ethical threat arises because employment contracts take precedence over ethical codes
The firm can automatically double its audit fees due to improved communication channels
e: A former partner joining a client as CEO creates severe familiarity and intimidation threats, often requiring significant cooling-off periods and restructuring of the engagement team.

q: Under the IESBA Code, can an audit firm provide recruitment services for key management positions to an audit client that is a PIE?
o: No, searching for or seeking out candidates for director or executive roles is strictly prohibited
Yes, provided the fee charged for recruitment is less than ten percent of total audit billings
Yes, provided the candidates are restricted to former employees of the audit firm itself
Yes, if the audit client board of directors signs a blanket liability waiver in advance
e: Providing recruitment services for director or senior management positions is prohibited for PIE audit clients because it involves participating in management decision-making.

q: Which of the following represents an advocacy threat for an accounting firm?
o: Representing an audit client in a formal tax dispute before an administrative tribunal or tax court
Conducting an objective count of physical inventory at the client remote warehouse locations
Issuing a qualified audit opinion due to an unresolved disagreement over asset valuations
Testing the internal operating effectiveness of routine purchase order approval controls
e: Acting as an advocate for an audit client in resolving a dispute or litigation before a court or tribunal creates an advocacy threat to objectivity.

q: Select the correct terms for the principle of professional behavior:
text: Accountants must comply with relevant [0] and avoid conduct that may [1] the profession.

q: What is meant by 'independence in mind' in the context of professional auditing?
o: The state of mind that permits expressing a conclusion without being affected by impairing influences
The external public perception that an auditor appears completely unbiased and honest
The mechanical adherence to a checklist of prohibited financial investments published by the regulator
The complete mental detachment from all knowledge of the client industry and competitive landscape
e: Independence in mind is the state of mind that permits the expression of a conclusion without being affected by influences that compromise professional judgment.

q: What ethical concept describes the overarching duty of professional accountants to serve beyond the immediate interests of their individual clients?
Under the IESBA Code, when may a professional accountant use confidential client information for personal advantage?
o: Never, using confidential information for personal advantage is strictly prohibited
Whenever the information relates to publicly listed shares traded on regulated exchanges
Provided the financial profit gained from the information does not exceed statutory thresholds
Only after the professional engagement has formally concluded and the client has dissolved
e: A professional accountant must not use or disclose confidential information for the personal advantage of the accountant or third parties under any circumstances.

q: Under the IESBA NOCLAR provisions, what is the ultimate responsibility of a senior professional accountant in business if management fails to act on severe illegal acts?
o: Determine whether disclosure to an appropriate external authority is needed in the public interest
Accept management decision without further action because loyalty to the employer is absolute
Charge an indemnity premium on future monthly salary payments to cover potential legal risks
Destroy all internal accounting records to shield the organization from judicial discovery
e: Under NOCLAR, if management fails to act, a senior PAIB must determine whether further action is needed, including disclosing the matter to an appropriate external authority in the public interest.

q: Which situation describes a self-review threat for an internal auditor in an enterprise?
o: Auditing internal controls over financial reporting that the internal auditor designed and implemented last year
Performing routine surprise cash counts at retail branch locations in accordance with the annual plan
Reviewing travel and entertainment expense claims submitted by middle management marketing personnel
Assisting external statutory auditors by providing completed workpapers on inventory verification tests
e: A self-review threat occurs when an internal auditor evaluates systems, controls, or procedures that they designed, implemented, or previously operated.

q: How does the IESBA Code view personal loans from an audit client that is a commercial bank?
o: Permitted if made under normal lending procedures, terms, and conditions, and not material
Strictly prohibited under all circumstances regardless of lending terms or commercial standards
Permitted only if granted at zero interest and without requirement of collateral backing
Allowed only if approved in advance by a national securities and exchange regulatory board
e: Loans from a bank audit client are permitted provided they are made under normal lending procedures, terms, and conditions (arm's length) and do not create material exposure.

q: When an accountant identifies an inadvertent breach of an independence provision, the firm must promptly discuss the breach with those charged with ______ at the client.
What ethical threat arises if an audit firm's fees for the current year are heavily dependent on selling non-audit consulting services to the audit client?
o: Self-interest threat
Advocacy threat
Intimidation threat exclusively
No threat arises if consulting staff are separate
e: Selling lucrative non-audit services to an audit client creates a significant self-interest threat, as the firm may fear losing consulting revenue if it challenges management on audit matters.

q: Under corporate governance best practices, why should the head of internal audit report functionally to the audit committee?
o: To ensure independence from executive management and maintain objectivity in audit reporting
To allow the audit committee to set the daily operational schedules of all accounting staff
To eliminate the requirement for external statutory audits under international regulatory statutes
To ensure that internal audit findings are kept secret from external regulatory examiners
e: Functional reporting to the audit committee safeguards internal audit independence and objectivity from executive management whom they evaluate.

q: Which ethical principle is compromised when an accountant knowingly signs off on a financial statement that overstates revenues to satisfy loan covenants?
o: Integrity and professional behavior
Confidentiality exclusively
Professional competence exclusively
No principle is breached if lenders are informed
e: Knowingly signing off on false or misleading financial statements breaches integrity (honesty and truthfulness) and professional behavior (discrediting the profession).

q: What ethical conflict arises when a professional accountant in business is pressured by executive directors to accelerate revenue recognition?
o: An intimidation and self-interest threat undermining the principles of integrity and objectivity
A familiarity threat arising from excessive collaboration with sales and logistics departments
An advocacy threat involving representation of corporate tax positions before civil authorities
A compliance conflict that can be remedied simply by reclassifying revenue as deferred income
e: Pressure from superiors creates intimidation and self-interest threats (fear of dismissal or bonus loss), threatening integrity and objectivity.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the significance of the 'reasonable and informed third party' test?
o: It serves as an objective benchmark to evaluate whether threats to independence are acceptable
It allows the audit firm to survey random retail consumers regarding the brand image of the client
It provides a legal mechanism for third-party creditors to inspect confidential audit working papers
It requires three independent accounting firms to co-sign the statutory audit report for PIEs
e: The test evaluates whether a reasonable and informed third party, weighing all facts and circumstances available at the time, would likely reach the same conclusion regarding independence.

q: Which factor must an audit firm evaluate when considering whether low-balling audit fees compromises ethical principles?
o: Whether the fee is so low that it impairs the firm ability to perform the audit in accordance with standards
Whether the client competitor firms are paying higher statutory audit fees for similar asset sizes
Whether the discounted fee forces the audit firm to lay off administrative office support personnel
Whether the audit engagement was won through a public electronic procurement portal or private tender
e: A low fee is not inherently unethical, but it creates a self-interest threat if it is so low that it impairs the firm's ability to assign competent staff and perform the audit in compliance with standards.

q: Under the IESBA Code, when may an audit firm provide tax planning services to an audit client?
o: When the tax treatment has a clear basis in tax law and does not involve aggressive tax planning
Whenever the tax savings generated exceed the total audit fees charged by the firm for the year
Only if the engagement partner is a certified attorney registered with the national supreme court
Under no circumstances, as all tax services are strictly prohibited for assurance clients
e: Tax planning services are permitted if they have a clear basis in tax law or established practice and do not involve aggressive tax avoidance or management decision-making.

q: What is the primary ethical issue when an auditor accepts an expensive holiday trip paid for by an audit client?
o: It creates significant self-interest and familiarity threats that cannot be reduced by any safeguards
It violates corporate travel entertainment guidelines unless the auditor travels economy class
It requires the auditor to reimburse the client company within sixty days of the trip conclusion
It is fully acceptable provided the auditor includes the hospitality value in taxable gross income
e: Accepting lavish gifts or hospitality cannot be justified as trivial or inconsequential, creating severe self-interest and familiarity threats that cannot be mitigated by safeguards.

q: Professional accountants are permitted to use confidential client information for personal financial advantage if it causes no financial loss to the client.
Under the IESBA Code, what safeguard is appropriate when a former audit team member is employed by the client in a non-accounting administrative role?
o: Assessing whether the former member can exert significant influence over the financial statements
Resigning immediately from the statutory audit engagement without discussing the matter with TCWG
Demanding that the former employee be terminated by the client prior to commencing fieldwork
Issuing an immediate qualified audit opinion due to an irremediable conflict of interest
e: If the individual cannot exert significant influence over the financial statements and subject matter, the threat is typically low and can be managed through engagement staffing adjustments.

q: Match each safeguard type with its organizational level:
left: Code of conduct and ethics training programs
Audit committee oversight and private meetings
Mandatory quality assurance reviews by regulatory body
right: Firm-wide safeguard
Engagement-specific safeguard
Client-level governance safeguard
Profession and regulatory safeguard

q: Under IESBA rules on NOCLAR, which of the following matters is specifically EXCLUDED from the scope of NOCLAR provisions?
o: Personal misconduct of client personnel unrelated to the financial operations of the entity
Non-compliance with environmental protection legislation impacting material contingent liabilities
Fraud, corruption, and bribery involving executive directors and key operational managers
Breaches of public health and safety regulations that could result in entity shutdown
e: NOCLAR does not cover matters that are clearly inconsequential or personal misconduct unrelated to the financial reporting or business activities of the employing entity or client.

q: When a professional accountant discovers that a client is involved in international terrorist financing, what overrides client confidentiality?
o: Statutory anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism legislation mandating immediate disclosure
The client commercial code of business conduct authorizing voluntary external arbitration
A verbal request from an investigative journalist conducting an industry expository article
The firm internal policy manual recommending public press releases on all criminal acts
e: Statutory reporting duties under anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws override client confidentiality, obligating disclosure to financial intelligence authorities.

q: What ethical concern arises when an audit firm agrees to calculate the deferred tax balances for a PIE audit client?
o: It creates an unacceptable self-review threat as the auditor would subsequently audit its own work
It breaches antitrust regulations governing the provision of corporate clerical assistance
It requires the firm to assume full legal liability for any future tax assessments and penalties
It is acceptable without restriction because deferred taxation is a mechanical calculation
e: Preparing accounting entries and calculations for deferred tax for a PIE creates a self-review threat that cannot be safeguarded against, as the firm audits its own calculations.

q: How many distinct core steps form the IESBA conceptual framework process (Identify, Evaluate, Address)?
Under the IESBA Code, how does secondment of audit firm personnel to an audit client affect independence?
o: It creates self-review and familiarity threats if the seconded staff make management decisions
It is prohibited under all circumstances regardless of the role or duration of the assignment
It automatically enhances audit quality by giving the audit firm direct operational control
It eliminates the necessity for management representation letters at year-end completion
e: Loaning personnel to an audit client creates self-review, familiarity, and advocacy threats, especially if personnel assume management responsibilities or prepare records that the firm audits.

q: Which situation illustrates an ethical dilemma involving the principle of professional competence?
o: An audit partner accepting an engagement in a specialized crypto-asset industry without adequate training
An accountant disclosing client turnover data to a bank with explicit written client authorization
A practitioner declining a complex engagement due to a lack of available senior technical staff
A financial controller reconciling monthly intercompany accounts in accordance with corporate IFRS manuals
e: Accepting an engagement without having or acquiring the required competence breaches the fundamental principle of professional competence and due care.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the role of 'Those Charged With Governance' (TCWG) regarding auditor independence?
o: They serve as an oversight body with whom the auditor communicates key independence threats and safeguards
They manage the daily operational accounting entries of the firm to ensure continuous compliance
They approve the personal tax returns of all individual audit team members before report signing
They guarantee the legal defense of the audit firm in the event of shareholder derivative suits
e: TCWG (such as the audit committee) provide governance oversight; auditors must communicate significant independence threats and applied safeguards to them.

q: Why is 'opinion shopping' considered a threat to professional ethics in the accounting industry?
o: It exerts intimidation and self-interest pressure on existing auditors to compromise on accounting treatments
It allows corporate clients to pay lower advertising costs for published statutory financial statements
It requires regulatory authorities to conduct mandatory re-audits of every entity that changes firms
It forces accounting firms to merge their international networks to maintain competitive pricing
e: Opinion shopping pressures existing auditors to compromise on accounting standards out of fear of being replaced by a firm willing to provide a favorable opinion.

q: Memorize the pairings between each ethical vulnerability and its threat category:
Which of the following non-audit services is generally PROHIBITED for a Public Interest Entity audit client under IESBA rules?
options: Assuming management responsibility for accounting systems
Reviewing interim tax returns prepared by client
Attending client audit committee meetings as observer
correct: Assuming management responsibility for accounting systems

q: Under international ethical guidance, what must an accountant do when faced with conflicting loyalties between employer and professional standards?
o: Professional ethical standards and the public interest must take precedence over employer demands
Employer directives must always prevail because the employment contract is legally binding
The accountant should follow employer orders but demand a written waiver of personal liability
The accountant should resign immediately without attempting any internal dispute resolution
e: Professional accountants have an overarching duty to the public interest and professional ethical standards, which must prevail over employer instructions that breach the Code.

q: What is the primary ethical danger of an audit firm participating in marketing or business development alliances with an audit client?
o: It creates a material commercial relationship that generates mutual self-interest and advocacy threats
It requires the accounting firm to register as an authorized financial securities broker-dealer
It infringes upon national antitrust rules prohibiting joint venture alliances among corporations
It transfers ownership of client intellectual property to the international audit partnership
e: Joint business ventures or alliances create close commercial relationships that generate severe self-interest and advocacy threats to objectivity and independence.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the mandatory requirement if an audit partner is offered a commercial loan on non-market terms by an audit client?
o: The partner must decline the loan because non-market terms create an impermissible self-interest threat
The partner may accept the loan provided the interest rate discount is reported to the tax authorities
The partner can accept the loan if the funds are used exclusively for personal residential property
The partner is permitted to accept if the client board of directors approves the loan unanimous vote
e: Loans not made under normal lending procedures, terms, and conditions create a self-interest threat that cannot be reduced to an acceptable level; they are strictly prohibited.

q: How does an audit firm address an inadvertent violation of an independence provision of the IESBA Code?
o: Identify and correct the breach, assess its significance, discuss with TCWG, and implement remedial action
Conceal the breach internally until the statutory statute of limitations on civil litigation expires
Automatically withdraw from the engagement without evaluating whether the breach was immaterial
Publish a formal public retraction in an international business journal within twenty-four hours
e: The IESBA Code sets out a protocol for breaches: terminate the interest/action, evaluate significance, discuss with TCWG, take remedial action, or withdraw if independence cannot be preserved.

q: Which ethical safeguard is most effective when an audit senior discovers that their brother is the head of procurement at an audit client?
o: Removing the audit senior from the engagement team and assigning a substitute senior
Instructing the senior to avoid testing any procurement transactions during the fieldwork
Requiring the senior brother to resign his procurement position prior to audit sign-off
Having the client chief executive officer supervise the audit senior procurement testing
e: Removing the individual from the audit team completely eliminates the familiarity and self-interest threats arising from close family ties.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the ethical concern when an audit firm prepares financial statements for a private (non-PIE) audit client?
o: It creates a self-review threat that requires safeguards such as using staff outside the audit team
It is an irremediable conflict that is universally prohibited across all corporate categories
It eliminates the client responsibility for financial statements under corporate company law
It allows the firm to issue an audit opinion without performing standard substantive tests
e: For non-PIEs, routine accounting and bookkeeping services are permitted if the self-review threat is reduced to an acceptable level (e.g., using different personnel) and client retains responsibility.

q: Swipe LEFT for Unacceptable Ethical Behaviors and RIGHT for Acceptable Ethical Behaviors:

What is the primary ethical role of professional bodies in maintaining public confidence in the accounting profession?
o: Enforcing disciplinary procedures, setting qualification benchmarks, and upholding ethical codes
Setting mandatory retail price minimums for professional accounting and taxation services
Lobbying national parliaments to exempt chartered accountants from corporate income tax
Purchasing controlling equity stakes in major national commercial banks and insurers
e: Professional bodies maintain public trust by establishing educational standards, issuing enforceable ethical codes, and operating investigation and disciplinary mechanisms.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what type of non-assurance service involves 'assuming management responsibility'?
o: Authorizing transactions, controlling bank accounts, or directing operational employee duties
Presenting comparative accounting policy options with benchmarked industry research data
Explaining the mechanical calculations behind statutory depreciation schedules to staff
Providing feedback on the grammatical readability of corporate sustainability disclosures
e: Assuming management responsibility involves making decisions, authorizing transactions, controlling assets, or setting policies, which no audit firm can do for an audit client.

q: Why is an auditor prohibited from acting as an advocate for an audit client in resolving a dispute with tax authorities?
o: Advocating a client position in an adversarial proceeding fundamentally undermines auditor objectivity
Tax authorities require all corporate disputes to be represented solely by licensed barristers
Advocating a position automatically converts the audit firm into a commercial subsidiary of the client
The firm would be required to forfeit all prior year audit fees under national tax statutes
e: Advocacy creates a mindset incompatible with objectivity, as the firm actively argues and defends the client's position in a public or formal adversarial setting.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is required before an audit firm accepts an engagement to provide non-assurance services to an audit client?
o: Ensure management designates an individual with suitable skill, knowledge, and experience to oversee services
Obtain an explicit legal indemnity that protects the audit firm from civil shareholder lawsuits
Require that the audit committee pay all consulting fees entirely in advance of service delivery
Transfer thirty percent of the engagement staff permanently onto the client corporate payroll
e: To avoid assuming management responsibility, the firm must be satisfied that client management designates a competent individual to oversee the service, evaluate results, and accept responsibility.

q: When a professional accountant encounters actual or suspected illegal acts involving senior leadership, to whom should they initially escalate internally?
o: The audit committee or those charged with governance of the organization
The lowest ranking clerical staff in the affected operational department
The external public relations consultant representing the corporate board
The personal legal counsel of the chief executive officer under attorney privilege
e: Escalation must be directed to higher levels of authority, specifically the audit committee or TCWG, who are independent of the involved senior management.

q: Under the principle of confidentiality, how long does an accountant duty to keep client data confidential persist after the professional relationship ends?
o: Indefinitely, continuing after the cessation of the relationship between accountant and client
For exactly twelve months following the issuance of the final statutory financial statements
Until the client company files its subsequent annual corporate tax return with the treasury
Only until the professional accountant secures new employment at a competing accounting firm
e: The duty of confidentiality continues indefinitely, even after the professional or business relationship has ended.

q: Select the correct terms for the impact of overdue audit fees:
text: Significant overdue fees create a [0] threat as the unpaid balance resembles a [1] to the client.

q: What ethical risk is introduced when an accounting firm receives significant referral fees or commissions for recommending third-party financial software?
o: A self-interest threat that may compromise the objectivity of the professional advice given
A familiarity threat arising from excessive contact with software developer engineering staff
An intimidation threat created by national consumer software distribution antitrust regulations
An advocacy threat requiring the accounting firm to guarantee the software against defects
e: Referral commissions create a self-interest threat because the accountant may recommend products based on personal financial gain rather than the client's best interests.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the rule regarding an audit firm providing internal audit services to a Public Interest Entity (PIE) audit client?
o: Strictly prohibited if the internal audit services relate to internal accounting controls or financial systems
Permitted provided the internal audit fees are lower than the statutory external audit fees
Permitted if the external audit team simply adopts the internal audit workpapers without testing
Allowed only if the client chief executive officer directly supervises every internal audit field visit
e: For PIEs, providing internal audit services that relate to the internal accounting controls, financial systems, or financial statements is strictly prohibited due to significant self-review threats.

q: What term describes an attitude that includes a questioning mind, being alert to conditions which may indicate possible misstatement, and a critical assessment of evidence?
Which of the following is considered an acceptable safeguard to mitigate an intimidation threat from an aggressive client CFO?
o: Involving an additional professional accountant who is not a member of the audit team to review the work
Capitulating to the CFO demands on accounting adjustments to avoid contentious disputes
Withholding all communication with the client audit committee until litigation is formally filed
Increasing the engagement team overtime hours to complete fieldwork ahead of the scheduled deadline
e: Involving an independent reviewing partner or another experienced professional to review work done provides an objective counterweight to client intimidation.

q: What ethical concern arises when an audit partner is invited to join the board of an audit client while still serving on the audit?
o: An absolute conflict of interest creating insurmountable self-review and self-interest threats
A minor familiarity threat that can be resolved by signing an annual independence waiver
An advocacy threat that only applies if the client issues new shares during the audit period
No conflict arises because board membership enhances the auditor understanding of business risks
e: Serving as an officer or director of an audit client creates insurmountable self-interest and self-review threats; an auditor cannot serve on the board of an assurance client.

q: A professional accountant must not allow bias, conflict of interest, or ______ influence of others to override professional judgment.
If an accountant suspects that money laundering is occurring, anti-money laundering legislation typically obligates them to report it without tipping off the client.
Match each independence concept with its definition:
right: State of mind allowing unbiased professional judgment
Avoidance of facts creating perception of bias to third parties
Partner responsible for decision-making on significant audit matters
Listed entity or entity defined by law as having significant public interest

q: Under the IESBA Code, why are contingent fees for preparation of tax returns generally prohibited or severely restricted?
o: They create an incentive to report biased figures to minimize tax liabilities for higher fees
They breach national revenue service regulations regarding standard legal hourly billings
They prevent tax authorities from conducting statutory tax audits on corporate returns
They force the professional firm to share tax refund proceeds with external creditors
e: Contingent fees based on the outcome of a tax return or tax controversy create a self-interest threat to objectivity and compliance with tax laws.

q: What constitutes a 'public interest entity' (PIE) under the revised IESBA Code of Ethics?
o: All listed entities and entities defined by regulation as such, including banks and insurers
Any commercial enterprise that employs more than fifty full-time salaried employees
Only state-owned utilities that receive direct operating subsidies from the government
Every charitable organization that solicits voluntary donations from the general public
e: A PIE includes all listed entities, entities whose shares/debt are traded on public markets, and other entities defined by law or regulation (often large financial institutions, pension funds).

q: Under the IESBA Code, how does the receipt of an inheritance of shares in an audit client by an audit team member need to be handled?
o: The shares must be disposed of at the earliest practical date and the individual removed from the team until then
The team member may retain the shares indefinitely provided they are placed in a safe deposit box
The firm must immediately resign from the statutory audit engagement without evaluating the holding
The shares must be transferred to the lead engagement partner to hold in trust until audit completion
e: If an audit team member inherits shares in an audit client, the financial interest must be disposed of at the earliest practical date and the individual must be removed from the engagement until disposal.

q: Which action represents a breach of the principle of professional competence and due care by an external auditor?
o: Failing to document substantive testing procedures while relying on unsubstantiated oral assurances
Requesting written confirmation of account balances directly from third-party banking institutions
Attending mandatory annual technical training updates on revised international auditing standards
Utilizing computerized audit data analytics tools to identify unusual journal entry transactions
e: Failing to document work and relying blindly on oral management representations without verification breaches due care and professional skepticism.

q: Under corporate governance principles, what is the primary role of an independent non-executive director (NED)?
o: Provide constructive challenge, strategic guidance, and monitor executive management performance
Execute the daily operational commercial contracts and sign routine employee payroll checks
Serve as the lead trial attorney in all corporate litigation brought by government agencies
Calculate the daily closing net asset values for all treasury short-term investment accounts
e: Independent NEDs provide detached oversight, constructively challenge strategy, evaluate executive performance, and safeguard shareholder and stakeholder interests.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what must a professional accountant do if offered an inducement that is NOT trivial and inconsequential?
o: Decline the inducement and take steps to avoid any association with improper influence
Accept the inducement and donate forty percent of its value to a recognized local charity
Retain the inducement after obtaining verbal approval from the client chief financial officer
Auction the inducement among firm audit staff and allocate proceeds to the annual staff party
e: If an inducement is made with intent to improperly influence or is not trivial and inconsequential, it must be declined immediately.

q: What is the typical fee dependency alert threshold (in percentage) for a PIE audit client under revised IESBA rules where fees exceed this level for two consecutive years?
What ethical threat arises when an audit firm designs and implements an IT accounting system that generates the financial statements?
o: Severe self-review threat and assumption of management responsibility
Familiarity threat resulting from daily interactions with IT hardware technicians
Advocacy threat requiring the audit firm to defend the software in legal proceedings
No threat arises if the accounting software is written in modern programming languages
e: Designing and implementing IT systems that generate source data or financial figures creates severe self-review threats and can involve assuming management responsibilities.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the restriction on an audit partner serving on the audit committee of an audit client?
o: Strictly prohibited because an audit partner cannot participate in governance of the audited entity
Permitted provided the partner abstains from voting on the appointment of the statutory auditor
Allowed only if the audit partner receives no compensation for serving on the audit committee
Permitted if the client shareholders pass a resolution with a seventy-five percent supermajority
e: Serving on the audit committee or board of an audit client involves holding a governance role, which directly impairs independence and is strictly prohibited.

q: Which scenario illustrates an ethical conflict of interest between two clients of the same accounting firm?
o: The firm provides advisory services to two competing corporate bidders competing to acquire the same target
The firm audits two separate manufacturing entities operating in entirely distinct geographic nations
The firm prepares routine tax returns for a retail grocery chain and an unrelated commercial airline
The firm conducts independent inventory counts for two independent local hardware distributors
e: Advising two competing bidders on the same acquisition creates an acute conflict of interest, as the firm cannot act in the best interests of both without compromising objectivity or confidentiality.

q: Memorize the pairings between each governance party and their ethical responsibility:

pairs.Those Charged with Governance: Oversee external auditor independence and integrity of reporting
pairs.External Auditor: Express independent opinion free from bias and conflict
pairs.Internal Auditor: Provide independent assurance to audit committee on internal controls
pairs.Chief Executive Officer: Set the tone at the top for corporate ethical conduct

q: Under the IESBA Code, how can a firm manage a conflict of interest between two competing commercial clients?
o: Disclose the conflict to both clients, obtain their informed consent, and establish strict information barriers
Terminate the client that pays lower annual consulting fees without providing any formal explanation
Share confidential pricing models between both clients to promote fair market competition
Instruct the lead partners of both teams to merge their working paper files into a shared archive
e: Managing client conflicts requires disclosure, informed consent, and safeguards like separate engagement teams, physical/electronic information barriers ('Chinese walls'), and independent oversight.

q: What is the primary danger when an accountant engages in 'creative accounting' within the technical boundaries of GAAP?
o: It misleads financial statement users and violates the fundamental principle of integrity
It automatically triggers an immediate criminal indictment under national penal legislation
It prevents the corporate entity from taking commercial tax deductions for depreciation
It forces the accounting firm to convert its legal partnership into a joint stock company
e: Aggressive or creative accounting that adheres to the letter but subverts the spirit of GAAP misleads users, compromising integrity and fair presentation.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the role of professional skepticism when evaluating management accounting estimates?
o: Critically assessing assumptions and corroborating evidence rather than accepting estimates unquestioningly
Assuming management is inherently dishonest and rejecting all internal operational estimates
Replacing all management estimates with historical five-year trailing industry average ratios
Delegating the assessment of all complex balance sheet estimates entirely to external legal counsel
e: Professional skepticism requires critical evaluation of evidence, questioning management assumptions, and being alert to management bias in subjective accounting estimates.

q: What ethical breach occurs if a professional accountant claims expertise in international tax treaties when they have no relevant training?
o: Breach of professional competence and due care, and breach of professional behavior
Breach of client confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations exclusively
Breach of the conceptual framework regarding familiarity threats
No breach occurs if the accountant hires an intern to research the tax treaties
e: Making exaggerated or false claims regarding qualifications and expertise violates professional competence and due care, as well as professional behavior.

q: Under anti-money laundering frameworks, what is meant by the prohibition against 'tipping off'?
o: Informing a suspect or third party that a suspicious activity report has been submitted to authorities
Advising a commercial client on how to optimize their legitimate annual corporate income tax returns
Alerting the engagement partner about an upcoming external regulatory quality control inspection
Disclosing the identity of the statutory audit team members in the published annual report
e: Tipping off is a criminal offense under AML laws where a person discloses that a suspicious activity report (SAR) has been filed or that an AML investigation is underway.

q: Which of the following would NOT be considered a Public Interest Entity under typical IESBA criteria?
options: Publicly listed conglomerate on a national stock exchange
Major retail bank with millions of depositor accounts
Small private family bakery with two retail branches
correct: Small private family bakery with two retail branches

q: Why does the IESBA Code prohibit an audit firm from entering into a contingent fee arrangement for non-assurance services to an audit client?
o: The firm outcome-dependent financial stake creates an unacceptable self-interest threat to audit objectivity
Contingent fees are prohibited under standard corporate contract law in every global jurisdiction
It requires the firm to pay thirty percent of the resulting fee to national securities regulators
It forces the client audit committee to assume joint criminal liability for consulting work
e: Even for non-assurance services, contingent fees from an audit client create an unacceptable self-interest threat, as the firm has a direct financial stake in the outcome.

q: Swipe LEFT for Self-Review Threats and RIGHT for Familiarity Threats:
What is the ethical requirement when an audit team member receives an employment offer from the audit client during the audit?
o: The team member must immediately notify the firm and be removed from the audit engagement team
The team member may remain on the audit provided they do not mention the offer to other assistants
The firm must issue an immediate disclaimer of opinion on the client financial statements
The client must compensate the audit firm by paying an executive recruitment placement fee
e: A team member negotiating employment with an audit client faces an acute self-interest threat; policies must require immediate disclosure and prompt removal from the audit team.

q: Under corporate governance codes, what is the primary role of an organization's audit committee regarding external auditors?
o: Reviewing auditor independence, recommending appointment, and overseeing the audit process
Performing the detailed substantive testing of inventory and payroll records alongside staff
Negotiating commercial sales discounts on company products sold to the audit firm partners
Preparing the original trial balance and drafting the notes to the financial statements
e: The audit committee oversees the relationship with the external auditor, assesses auditor independence, monitors the effectiveness of the audit, and recommends appointment/retention.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the required mindset when applying the conceptual framework to an ethical situation?
o: Exercising professional judgment, remaining alert to new information, and applying the reasonable third party test
Strictly executing a pre-printed checklist without exercising qualitative professional evaluation
Following the verbal directives of the client board chairman regardless of professional standards
Assuming that all ethical dilemmas can be solved by adjusting the financial materiality threshold
e: Applying the conceptual framework requires professional judgment, awareness of changes in facts/circumstances, and using the reasonable and informed third party test.

q: What ethical risk is posed when an audit firm relies heavily on automated artificial intelligence tools for substantive audit testing?
o: Over-reliance without exercising human professional skepticism, understanding models, or verifying inputs
Breach of international copyright treaties governing commercial database software licensing
Mandatory reclassification of the audit firm as a software development enterprise under tax codes
Loss of the firm statutory authority to sign the independent audit opinion under company law
e: Using AI without sufficient competence, critical review, and professional skepticism creates threats to professional competence, due care, and objectivity through automation bias.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what should an accountant do if they face intimidation threats involving threats of physical harm?
o: Prioritize personal safety, notify law enforcement authorities, and seek legal and professional counsel
Continue working on the engagement while attempting to conceal the threats from firm management
Offer to modify the audit opinion in exchange for guaranteed physical security from the client
Publish an unredacted copy of the working papers on social media networks immediately
e: Physical threats compromise safety and objectivity; the accountant must prioritize personal safety, report to law enforcement, notify firm leadership, and seek legal advice.

q: Unscramble the term for the fundamental ethical principle of avoiding bias and prejudice in judgment:
Which fundamental principle is demonstrated when an accountant refuses to accept a lucrative bonus that is conditional on signing off on fraudulent revenue?
o: Integrity and objectivity
Confidentiality exclusively
Professional competence exclusively
No principle is involved as bonuses are purely contractual matters
e: Refusing corrupt financial incentives to maintain honest and unbiased reporting demonstrates integrity (truthfulness) and objectivity (uncompromised judgment).

q: Select the correct terms regarding improper inducements:
text: Accountants offered an improper inducement must [0] the offer and inform [1] or law enforcement.

q: Under IESBA Part 4A, how does the Code differentiate between an audit of a Public Interest Entity (PIE) and a non-PIE regarding non-assurance services?
o: Stricter prohibitions apply to PIEs, generally banning services that create self-review threats
Non-PIEs are subject to mandatory partner rotation every three years, whereas PIEs are exempt
PIEs may receive routine bookkeeping services without any requirement for separate staffing
No distinction exists because all assurance clients are subject to identical independence rules
e: The IESBA Code applies significantly stricter independence rules to PIEs, prohibiting non-assurance services that create self-review threats (e.g., accounting/bookkeeping, valuations affecting financials).

q: What constitutes an 'indirect financial interest' that is prohibited under the IESBA Code for an audit team member?
o: An investment in an intermediary fund where the auditor has control or the interest is material
An immaterial holding in a diversified mutual fund over which the auditor has zero control
A personal checking deposit account with a commercial bank audit client that is fully insured
A home mortgage loan obtained on standard commercial market terms from an audit client bank
e: An indirect financial interest is prohibited if it is material to the investor or if the investor has control over the investment decisions of the intermediary vehicle.

q: What term describes the ethical principle where an accountant is prohibited from taking credit for another person's intellectual work?
Under IESBA standards, a firm must establish policies and procedures designed to provide it with reasonable assurance that the firm and its personnel maintain ______ when required.
Under the IESBA Code, what is the 'cooling-off period' requirement when an engagement partner moves directly from the audit firm to become CFO of a PIE audit client?
o: A mandatory period must elapse (often at least twelve months) before accepting such employment
The partner can start immediately provided they surrender their firm equity partnership interest
A twenty-four hour administrative hiatus is required between resigning and joining the client
No cooling-off period applies if the client audit committee unanimously approves the hiring
e: When a key audit partner joins a PIE client as an executive officer or director, the Code requires a cooling-off period (typically 12 months under IESBA, or longer locally) to mitigate familiarity/intimidation threats.

q: A professional accountant may assist an audit client in preparing accounting records provided the firm makes all managerial decisions on the client's behalf.
In an assurance engagement other than an audit or review (Part 4B), what level of independence is required?
o: Independence from the assurance client regarding the specific subject matter and assertions
Complete independence from all commercial suppliers and trade creditors of the entity
Zero independence requirements apply because Part 4B only covers voluntary consulting
Identical partner rotation requirements as those mandated for Public Interest Entities
e: Part 4B applies independence standards to other assurance engagements, requiring independence from the client regarding the specific subject matter and criteria being evaluated.

q: Under the NOCLAR framework, what is the primary factor an auditor in public practice considers before disclosing non-compliance to an external authority?
o: Whether disclosure is necessary to avoid serious harm to the public interest or stakeholders
Whether the client has agreed in writing to reimburse the firm for external legal counsel fees
Whether the audit firm can obtain media publicity that enhances its brand reputation
Whether the statutory statute of limitations has expired for civil shareholder litigation
e: Under NOCLAR, the auditor must determine if disclosure to an external authority is appropriate in the public interest, considering the nature and extent of serious harm to stakeholders.

q: Which scenario creates an unavoidable advocacy threat that cannot be eliminated by any safeguard?
o: An audit partner acting as the primary legal advocate for an audit client in a public court trial
An audit firm preparing statutory payroll calculations using data approved by client HR management
An audit senior attending an industry trade conference where client products are displayed
A firm tax partner answering routine questions raised by a revenue agent during an audit inquiry
e: Acting as an advocate for an audit client in resolving a dispute or litigation before a court or tribunal is prohibited because it compromises objectivity.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the consequence when an audit client threatens to replace the audit firm over a disputed accounting estimate?
o: An intimidation threat arises that requires firm leadership and TCWG involvement to manage
The auditor must immediately concede to management proposed valuation to preserve the engagement
The auditor must automatically issue an adverse opinion without completing substantive tests
The firm is legally compelled to file an immediate commercial bankruptcy petition on the client
e: Threatening replacement creates an intimidation threat; safeguards include consulting the firm technical department, engaging TCWG, or withdrawing if independence is impaired.

q: When may a professional accountant in business disclose confidential company data without management consent?
o: When required by statutory whistleblowing laws or subpoenaed by a court of competent jurisdiction
When seeking new employment at a competing firm to prove past professional accomplishments
When discussing financial performance with personal acquaintances on social media networks
Whenever the accountant believes the company current share price is trading above intrinsic value
e: Confidentiality exceptions exist where disclosure is required by law (e.g., statutory whistleblowing, judicial subpoenas) or when permitted under professional frameworks like NOCLAR.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is required if an audit firm provides corporate finance advice involving advice on the structure of an acquisition?
o: The service is prohibited if the advice has a material effect on the financial statements audited
The service is permitted unconditionally provided the corporate finance fees are capped at ten thousand dollars
The firm must assume joint ownership of the acquired entity for a minimum of two calendar years
The client board chairman must formally assign executive management voting powers to the audit partner
e: Providing corporate finance services creates advocacy and self-review threats; for PIEs, or where advice materially impacts the financial statements, it is prohibited.

q: Match each ethical terminology with its proper context:
right: Disclosing to a client that a suspicious activity report has been filed
Quoting an unrealistically low audit fee to win an engagement
Client seeking an auditor willing to accept an aggressive accounting treatment
Reporting misconduct to regulators or external law enforcement

q: What ethical concern arises when an audit firm accepts an engagement fee that is significantly lower than market rates?
o: A self-interest threat that the firm will compromise audit quality or omit necessary audit procedures
A familiarity threat arising from excessive empathy towards client cash flow constraints
An advocacy threat requiring the audit firm to defend client products against market rivals
An intimidation threat from competitor firms filing antitrust predatory pricing complaints
e: Undercharging creates a self-interest threat that the auditor will cut corners or fail to perform adequate testing to contain costs within the low fee budget.

q: Under the revised IESBA fee provisions, what is the threshold for a PIE where fee dependency triggers mandatory governance disclosure?
o: When total fees from the PIE client exceed 15% of total firm fees for two consecutive years
When total fees from the PIE client exceed 50% of total firm fees in any single calendar month
When audit fees from the PIE exceed the gross national product of the host operating country
When non-audit fees equal or exceed twice the statutory external audit fee in any single year
e: The IESBA Code mandates that if fees from a PIE exceed 15% of the firm's total fees for two consecutive years, disclosure to TCWG and external/pre-issuance reviews are required.

q: What is the primary purpose of an Engagement Quality Review (EQR) under ISQM 2 from an ethical perspective?
o: To provide an objective evaluation of significant judgments and conclusions before report release
To negotiate commercial billing rate discounts directly with client corporate treasury staff
To assume ultimate civil liability for any undetected misstatements in the balance sheet
To physically count all fixed assets and inventory across every overseas client location
e: An EQR provides an independent, objective evaluation of significant judgments and conclusions reached by the engagement team, acting as an important quality and ethical safeguard.

q: Under IESBA rules, for how many consecutive years may an individual serve as an Engagement Quality Reviewer (EQR) on a PIE audit before mandatory rotation?
Under the IESBA Code, what is the ethical issue with an audit partner having a close personal friendship with the client Chief Executive Officer?
o: It creates a familiarity threat that may cause the partner to be too sympathetic to client views
It creates an intimidation threat because the CEO will force the partner to perform free tax work
It creates an advocacy threat that requires the partner to buy shares in the client company
It eliminates the client legal obligation to prepare annual audited financial statements
e: Close personal relationships between engagement team leaders and client senior executives generate familiarity threats that can erode objectivity and professional skepticism.

q: How should an audit firm resolve a situation where an audit client refuses to correct a material fraudulent misstatement?
o: Express a qualified or adverse opinion, or withdraw from the engagement if legally permitted
Issue an unmodified clean opinion while retaining a confidential memo in internal files
Adjust the materiality threshold upward so that the fraudulent misstatement becomes immaterial
Accept a promissory note from the client management promising rectification in three years
e: If material fraudulent misstatements are uncorrected, the auditor must issue a modified opinion (qualified or adverse) or withdraw from the engagement, reporting to TCWG and authorities as appropriate.

q: What is the primary ethical danger of 'earnings management' orchestrated by corporate executives?
o: It distorts economic reality to deceive stakeholders, breaching the principle of integrity
It results in an automatic forfeiture of all accumulated corporate retained earnings under law
It requires the internal audit department to report directly to commercial debt rating agencies
It compels external auditors to assume legal ownership of all corporate treasury holdings
e: Earnings management manipulates financial reporting to mislead investors and creditors about true performance, directly violating integrity and objective financial reporting.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what restriction applies to recruiting services provided to an audit client that is NOT a PIE?
o: The firm must not act as a negotiator or make the hiring decision on behalf of the client
The firm can make the final hiring decision provided the fee is less than five thousand dollars
The firm is permitted to draft and sign the employment contracts as the client legal agent
The firm can hire its own engagement partners directly into executive client positions without notice
e: Even for non-PIEs, the firm cannot assume management responsibility; it can recommend candidates or interview them against criteria, but client management must make the hiring decision.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the role of 'whistleblower protection' policies in an organization?
o: To protect individuals who report illegal conduct or ethical breaches from detrimental treatment
To prevent external regulatory agencies from accessing internal confidential corporate memos
To ensure that senior executive compensation packages remain shielded from public disclosure
To allow employees to bypass all operational internal controls without disciplinary review
e: Whistleblower protection shields reporting employees from retaliation, termination, or harassment, ensuring ethical issues and legal violations can be brought to light.

q: What ethical conflict arises when an accountant in business is instructed to capitalize operating expenses to avoid a loan covenant breach?
o: An intimidation threat and self-interest threat forcing association with misleading statements
A familiarity threat arising from working closely with bank commercial loan officers
An advocacy threat requiring the accountant to negotiate lower interest rates on borrowings
A professional competence threat that can be resolved by taking an online bookkeeping refresher
e: Improperly capitalizing expenses to hide covenant breaches produces false financial statements, violating integrity, objectivity, and professional behavior under intimidation pressure.

q: Under the IESBA Code, how does the provision of valuation services to a PIE audit client impact independence?
o: It is prohibited if the valuation involves subjective judgment and has a material effect on financials
It is always permitted provided the valuation is calculated using discounted cash flow models
It is allowed if the valuation report is reviewed by a junior associate at a competing firm
It is mandatory under international accounting standards to ensure asset balance accuracy
e: Valuation services for PIEs that involve subjectivity and materially impact financial statements create insurmountable self-review threats and are strictly prohibited under the IESBA Code.

q: What constitutes a 'conflict of interest' for a professional accountant in public practice under Section 310?
o: Undertaking an activity that creates conflicting interests between two clients or client and firm
Charging standard commercial hourly billing rates for non-audit consulting engagements
Auditing two companies that operate in entirely different industries and geographical regions
Refusing to provide legal advocacy services for an assurance client in an appellate court
e: A conflict of interest arises when a professional accountant undertakes an activity where their interests or duties conflict with those of a client, or between two or more competing clients.

q: Under the IESBA Code, what is the consequence of an audit firm partner holding a direct financial interest in an audit client through a blind trust?
o: It is prohibited because beneficial ownership of a direct financial interest still impairs independence
It is permitted unconditionally because the partner does not manage the specific assets in the trust
It is allowed provided the trust assets represent less than twenty percent of the partner wealth
It is acceptable if the trust was established by the client corporate board of directors
e: Holding a direct financial interest through a blind trust does not eliminate the beneficial interest; it remains a direct financial interest and impairs independence.

q: What safeguard can an accounting firm apply when two competing clients seek advisory services on the same corporate acquisition?
o: Form separate advisory teams with strict electronic information barriers and written client consent
Advise both clients through a single unified engagement team to ensure identical valuation data
Recommend that one client withdraw immediately while charging them a standard cancellation fee
Disclose both bidders confidential financial projections to the target company board of directors
e: Safeguards include obtaining informed consent, using separate engagement teams with different partners/staff, establishing electronic information barriers ('Chinese walls'), and independent oversight.

q: Under the IESBA Code, how is the 'public interest' defined in relation to the accountancy profession?
o: The collective well-being of the community and institutions the professional accountant serves
The maximization of net accounting profits for audit firm equity partners and shareholders
The total market capitalization of companies listed on the national domestic stock exchange
The complete elimination of corporate tax obligations for private small business enterprises
e: A distinguishing mark of the profession is its acceptance of the responsibility to act in the public interest—the collective well-being of society, financial markets, and stakeholders.

q: What ethical threat arises when an audit firm assists an audit client in lobbying government officials for regulatory changes?
o: Advocacy threat
Self-review threat exclusively
Familiarity threat exclusively
No threat arises if lobbying expenses are disclosed
e: Lobbying on behalf of an audit client creates an advocacy threat, as the firm is publicly promoting and advancing the client's political and commercial agenda.

q: Memorize the pairings between each ethical pressure and its proper professional response:

pairs.Offer of expensive vacation from client: Decline gift and record in firm gift register
pairs.Threat of sacking if audit qualification: Consult technical partner and issue correct opinion
